subject: gov.policy
name: ADIGE digital agenda
milestone: The digital agenda the World Bank diagnostic assesses against
position_start: The stated digital agenda, with the diagnostic's recommendations outstanding
position_end: Launched 2019 by the Ministerio de Transportes, Correos y Telecomunicaciones on 33 lineas de accion running to 2025, aligned with the UN 2030 Agenda SDGs, the CPLP Digital Agenda and the African Union's Agenda 2063; unchanged since - no implementation report, budget figure or revised agenda is held
sources: 2024-06-25 Equatorial Guinea Digital Economy Country Diagnostic - Bridging the Gaps|2024-07-15 World Bank identifies priority actions for DPI in Equatorial Guinea|2022-03-27-guinea-ecuatorial-adige-agenda-digital
note: since padded to the launch year only (2019); no exact launch date is published

subject: gov.policy
name: Consolidated July-December 2026 action plan
milestone: Adopted by the second extraordinary directive council, 31 July 2026, and not yet financed
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Adopted with 35 strategic objectives under three national priorities, one of them restoring sovereignty over the national digital space; it goes to the interministerial council and then to the Council of Ministers, which decides what is recorded and funded
note: the plan document is not published; the government portal dates the council to 31 July and Real Equatorial Guinea to 30 July

subject: gov.policy
name: Electronic laws package 2015-2017
milestone: Five laws published together
position_start: In force (2025-08)
position_end: Five laws covering data protection, data retention, electronic signature, electronic access and internet communications, published together in the official bulletin and unamended since

subject: gov.policy
name: Governance of state-participation companies
milestone: Directorships filled by competitive interview with six-month provisional appointments
position_start: Appointments and board membership not on record as contested
position_end: Article 16 of the Ley Reguladora de Empresas Publicas invoked to remove supervising officeholders from parastatal boards, and director-general posts at GITGE, ANDEGE, INSESO and Gepetrol Servicios filled by competitive interview against stated criteria

subject: gov.policy
name: National broadband coverage target
milestone: 85 per cent coverage set for end-2026
position_start: No published broadband target (2025-08)
position_end: The transport ministry's half-year plan sets the country's first published target: 85 per cent second and fourth generation coverage through 34 new towers by the end of 2026 (2026-07)

subject: gov.policy
name: National digital strategy
milestone: Drafting session with the World Bank, September 2026
position_start: No national digital strategy, only the 2024 digital agenda (2025-08)
position_end: A World Bank team opened a four-day session in Malabo in September 2026 to finalise a national digital economy strategy, on a diagnostic that found no interoperability framework and no digital skills data held (2026-09)

subject: gov.policy
name: National fibre backbone
milestone: Four rings and an international gateway
position_start: A four-ring national fibre backbone with an international gateway, over US$30m invested (2019-01)
position_end: The electricity utility is studying whether to lease its own 2,000km grid fibre network to telecom operators, on a vendor study; a further ring modernisation sits inside the state operator's 2026-2030 plan (2026-06)

subject: gov.policy
name: Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2035
milestone: The framework the World Bank Country Economic Memorandum assesses
position_start: In force as the national development framework
position_end: In force; primary text recovered (Agenda Guinea Ecuatorial 2035 / ENDS 2035, successor to the Plan Horizonte 2020, no internal adoption date, uploaded 2024-05) commits to gradual privatisation of state telecom ownership, universal broadband backbone across all regions, an updated telecoms legal and regulatory framework, and a proposed Fondo de Apoyo a la Ciencia, Tecnologia e Innovacion (FACTI) that may be funded by a special tax on oil and gas exports; the World Bank's separately noted digital recommendations - a one-stop shop, online business registration and a digitised commercial registry - remain undelivered on record
sources: 2025-03-04 Country Economic Memorandum on Equatorial Guinea 2025 - Building Foundations for Renewed Diversified and Inclusive Growth|2024-05-01-guinea-ecuatorial-ends-2035-estrategia-desarrollo-sostenible
note: primary text has no internal adoption date; since is dated to the verifiable upload path (2024-05), per the source's own dating resolution

subject: gov.policy
name: Recovery of the .GQ country-code domain
milestone: A Comision Nacional de Negociacion named in the July-December 2026 plan
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A negotiating commission is to be created to recover the domain from a foreign operator the release does not name; nothing is established about the current administration arrangement

subject: gov.legislate
name: Ley 7/2024 on social media and computer crime
milestone: Four criminal complaints lodged 2026-09-16 at a Malabo investigating court
movement: Advanced, first prosecutions under the law
position_start: In force
position_end: In force, and used: on 16 September 2026 lawyers for the vice-president lodged four criminal complaints against a digital newspaper's journalist and three others under articles 2, 50 and 60, invoking article 2 to reach conduct outside national territory; the government had reasserted the law's full force in July 2026
note: the full text is not held; the provisions are known from reporting

subject: gov.legislate
name: National land cadastre law
milestone: Field census begun at Bata, June 2026
position_start: Land title on a concession basis with customary tenure registration optional, under the 2009 land law and an 1906 survey statute (2009-05)
position_end: Deputies approved a national land cadastre bill in May 2025 replacing the colonial-era survey law, and the first house-to-house cadastral census began at Bata in June 2026 (2026-06)

subject: gov.legislate
name: Press law revision
status: In development, before the Senate plenary
milestone: Senate committee approved its final report by consensus, reported 2026-10-08
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The press freedom and journalism bill replacing Law 6/1997 passed the Chamber of Deputies on 11 September 2026 and a Senate committee has sent it to the plenary by consensus; it gives digital journalists the same protections and duties, sets a right of access to public information and creates a college of journalists
note: no plenary vote, text or commencement date is published

subject: gov.legislate
name: Public sector contracts law and electronic procurement system
milestone: Enacted as Ley 11/2025 of 12 December 2025, reported 2026-01-08
position_start: No electronic procurement system and no governing statute (2025-08)
position_end: A bill creating an electronic public procurement information system went to the Senate for single-reading study in November 2025 (2025-11). Enacted as Ley 11/2025 of 12 December 2025 on public-sector contracts, which sets up the GE Compras electronic procurement information system for electronic submission and evaluation of bids and a mandatory public electronic register of state contractors and suppliers; the statute's own text is not held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Recoding of the national tax identification number
milestone: Draft decree before the interministerial council, August 2026
position_start: A tax identification number folded into the business single window since 2017 (2017-09)
position_end: A draft decree would recode the tax identification number for individuals, companies and unregistered entities alike - the first move to make it a general identifier rather than a company one (2026-08)

subject: gov.legislate
name: Reform of Ley 7/2005 General de Telecomunicaciones
milestone: International tender opened for a firm to draft a new law, June 2025
position_start: Tender opened, scoped to cover AI, cybersecurity, critical infrastructure, satellite connectivity and data protection
position_end: No award, draft or revised timetable has been published in the fourteen months since

subject: gov.legislate
name: Reform of the Ley de Prensa y Medios Audiovisuales (1997)
milestone: Draft provisions reported 2026-10-22
position_start: In force since 1997, with no provision for digital media or cable TV
position_end: Bill presented adding regulation of digital media and cable television for the first time, under committee review, with no adoption date or bill text published; a separate Copyright and Related Rights bill was presented alongside it, implementing Equatorial Guinea's 1997 Berne Convention accession and its 2015 Bangui Agreement obligations under OAPI. The draft reported on 2026-10-22 would ban content inciting violence, hatred or crime or harming minors across print, audiovisual and digital media, require streaming, podcast and digital-platform providers to register and answer for the content they carry, and oblige audiovisual licensees to give the regulator free monitoring of their broadcasts and retained recordings; its legislative stage is not stated
note: neither bill text is held; scope is as reported from the minister's appearance. The copyright provisions are a companion bill rather than part of the audiovisual bill, which the earlier record did not separate

subject: gov.legislate
name: Satellite broadband sales routed through the regulator
milestone: Decided at a working session, 2026-09-09
position_start: Not held
position_end: All sales of the satellite internet service are to run through the telecommunications regulator, under the supervision of the artificial intelligence state secretariat, and service contracts citizens obtained outside official channels are to be cancelled, decided at a working session led by the vice-president on 9 September 2026
note: the regulator is made the seller of a service it regulates; no instrument text is published

subject: gov.legislate
name: Social protection system law
milestone: Passed at second reading, March 2026
position_start: A bill under study, with the social insurance institute the only system held (2023-03)
position_end: The Senate passed the social protection bill at second reading in March 2026; no registry or management information system is specified in it (2026-03)

subject: gov.legislate
name: Taxation of foreign digital platforms
milestone: Talks ordered with a large platform, 2026-09-08
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The state intends a mechanism letting it capture part of the revenue large digital platforms generate in its market. The vice-president instructed a commission on 8 September 2026 in Malabo to open talks with one such platform, which he said has built its business in the country without paying the state, and with comparable platforms as alternatives.
note: an instruction to open talks, not an instrument: no draft law, rate, tax base, revenue estimate or platform response is published, and no assessment of what the platforms currently pay is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Transparency and access to information law
milestone: Passed unanimously by the Senate, May 2026
position_start: No access-to-information statute (2025-08)
position_end: The country's first transparency and access-to-information bill passed the Senate unanimously in May 2026, three months after the Prime Minister opened the debate; no publication scheme or portal follows from it yet (2026-05)

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection law and supervisory authority
milestone: Gazetted 22 July 2016, in force twenty days later
position_start: Not held
position_end: In force since 2016-08-11; gives rights of access, rectification, cancellation, opposition and indemnisation and a sanctions regime running to CFA 15,000,000 for the gravest infractions, but Article 15 leaves the Organo Rector de Proteccion de Datos Personales - and the registry it would run - to a decree the government has never issued; africadataprotection.org's own country page records no supervisory authority publicly identified
note: the Organo Rector was never created by the decree Article 15 requires

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection readiness
status: Enacted, no supervisory authority in operation
milestone: Ratification of the regional convention approved, March 2026
position_start: A 2016 data protection law with no operating supervisory authority (2025-08)
position_end: The Chamber of Deputies approved ratification of the African Union convention on cyber security and personal data protection in March 2026, four months before the signing ceremony; no supervisory authority is recorded as operating (2026-03)

subject: gov.regional
name: CEMAC Regional Financial Inclusion Strategy 2025-2029
milestone: Validated by the monetary union's ministerial committee 21 December 2023
position_start: Baseline not held
position_end: A 2025-2029 regional strategy adopted by the central bank for the six member states, validated by the monetary union's ministerial committee on 21 December 2023 and published in February 2025; the 83-page text is held in full
note: the strategy is regional and the repository holds no member-state implementation plan, target or outturn under it

subject: gov.regional
name: CPLP digital rights charter
milestone: Signed at São Tomé by all nine member states, 19 July 2024
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Expressly declaratory and non-binding, committing members to meaningful connectivity on non-discriminatory and affordable terms, personal data protection, cybersecurity cooperation, digital literacy and capacity building and non-fragmentation of the digital environment, and condemning blanket internet shutdowns
note: declaratory: no domestic measure is recorded as taken under it

subject: gov.regional
name: Lusophone Africa data governance process
milestone: Second Lusophone Africa Data Governance Workshop, Luanda, 15-17 June 2026
position_end: Participated at the second regional workshop applying UNESCO's Data Governance Toolkit; no national framework or commitment resulted on the record

subject: gov.regional
name: Malabo Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection
milestone: Signed at Addis Ababa, 28 July 2026
position_start: Neither signed nor ratified, per the African Union register as at 2026-02-02
position_end: Signatory since 28 July 2026 and not a party; no instrument of ratification is on file or on the AU register
note: the Chamber of Deputies' unanimous vote of 25 March 2026 was a domestic authorisation to ratify, taken before the country was a signatory

subject: gov.regional
name: Presidency of the Statistical Commission for Africa, 2026-2028
milestone: Elected at the tenth session, Addis Ababa, October 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The country chairs the UN regional statistical commission for 2026-2028, the session presided by the head of the national statistics institute

subject: gov.standards
name: AGENOR standards and certification agency
milestone: Seven-stage plan unveiled March 2025, agency pre-launch
position_start: A standards agency unveiling a seven-stage plan and still pre-launch (2025-03)
position_end: Malabo hosted an international telecommunications symposium in May 2026 whose declaration commits to interoperable standards for green digital infrastructure; the national agency itself remains pre-launch (2026-05)

subject: gov.standards
name: Published quality-of-service or interoperability standards
milestone: OM Num. 4/2018 gazetted 22 August 2018, confirmed via ORTEL's own legislacion index
position_start: Not held
position_end: Reglamento sobre Calidad Integral de Servicio en Materia de Prestacion de los Servicios de Comunicaciones Electronicas al Publico (OM Num. 4/2018) confirmed in force per ORTEL's own regulatory index; only the instrument's title and date are held, not its text
note: the index also lists a separate inspection/sanctions regulation (OM Num. 4/2020) and a February 2026 broadband-market update (OM Num. 1/2026), neither captured as a row here

subject: gov.discourse
name: Observatorio 2035 consultation body
milestone: Created by decree, composition deferred
position_start: Created on paper, never constituted (2025-08)
position_end: The decree adopting the national sustainable development strategy creates a consultation observatory and defers its composition; nothing records it meeting

subject: gov.discourse
name: Prosecution and anti-corruption commission coordination protocol
milestone: Agreed at a first institutional meeting, 2026-09-03
position_start: Not held
position_end: The attorney general's office and the national anti-corruption commission agreed a permanent coordination mechanism on 3 September 2026: institutional liaison points for continuous contact, an information-exchange protocol and periodic reviews (2026-09)
note: no protocol text, data categories, safeguards or first review date is published, and the exchange is between two bodies neither of which publishes a caseload

subject: finance.budget
name: Domestic budget appropriation for digital transformation
position_end: Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and AI Systems (Section 51) budgeted CFA 5,802,246 thousand for FY2026, down from CFA 7,556,246 thousand the prior year (-23%), 0.4% of the CFA 1,294,282m total budget; includes CFA 140,000 thousand for the Escuela de Telecomunicaciones Djibloho, per Ley 9/2025 of 9 December 2025 (Ejercicio 2026)
note: figures located by grep on the extracted budget text; the fuller Anexo IV/V detail was not read

subject: finance.mou
name: Huawei electronic government memorandum
milestone: Network optimisation contract signed July 2026
position_start: A video surveillance contract financed by a Chinese development bank loan (2019-01)
position_end: A memorandum to accelerate electronic government was signed in December 2025 with no financial terms disclosed; contract annexes closed in March 2026 adding plate recognition and 80 technicians to train in China; and the state operator signed a six-month network optimisation contract in July, value undisclosed (2026-07)

subject: finance.new
name: China Development Bank loan for the Video Surveillance Project
milestone: US$70.3m loan for the Video Surveillance Project
position_start: Committed
position_end: Unchanged; no delivery, siting or oversight arrangement for the surveillance system is on record

subject: finance.new
name: China Eximbank credit for the CEIBA-2 cable
milestone: US$402m buyer's credit for the CEIBA-2 submarine cable
position_start: Drawn, with the cable in service
position_end: Unchanged; no repayment or restructuring is on record

subject: finance.new
name: Private investment proposal for the second state operator
milestone: US$50m proposal received January 2026
position_start: State telecom assets listed for privatisation as a lending benchmark (2022-04)
position_end: A private group offered US$50m to launch the second state operator with a 49 per cent state stake in January 2026, and a Nigerian company signed a deal for a submarine cable and a commercial data centre in February with no figures disclosed (2026-02)

subject: infra.connect
name: ACE submarine cable landing
milestone: GITGE hosted the 36th ACE operation and maintenance committee, May 2026
position_start: Landing party for ACE through GITGE
position_end: Landing party for ACE; capacity unchanged on the record

subject: infra.connect
name: Block on Facebook and TikTok with throttled bandwidth
milestone: In force since 2026-09-02
position_start: Not held
position_end: Since 2 September 2026 bandwidth has been throttled and Facebook and TikTok unreachable without a VPN, with WhatsApp and Instagram working only partially, after a viral video accusing the vice-president of corruption whose author was arrested; the information ministry did not respond to questions
note: no government order or statement is held; the account is a news agency's

subject: infra.connect
name: Ceiba-1 and Ceiba-2 submarine cables
milestone: Ceiba-2 inaugurated in 2018, 400 km on the Malabo-Bata-Kribi route
position_start: In service, alongside the ACE landing
position_end: In service; no later capacity or utilisation figure is held
sources: 2018-06-06 Equatorial Guinea and Cameroon are now more connected - AFR-IX telecom

subject: infra.connect
name: Digital Terrestrial Television project
milestone: Tender published for a technical diagnostic and regularisation, 29 July 2026
position_start: Built but incomplete, with no published switchover date
position_end: Under tender for diagnostic, regularisation, rehabilitation, commissioning and operational transfer, Treasury-financed, with no contract value, deadline or switchover date published
note: the tender's terms of reference are not held; ahoraeg.com returns HTTP 403 to direct fetches

subject: infra.connect
name: Gabon-Equatorial Guinea fibre, roaming and frequency accords
milestone: Interconnection of the two national backbones inaugurated at Ebibeyin, 10 November 2025
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Physically and logically interconnected and inaugurated at Ebibeyin, with traffic exchanged on the Bitam-Ebibeyin and Libreville-Bata routes; the accords covering free roaming and frequency coordination are signed, and no traffic, capacity or tariff figure is published
note: The Gabonese state infrastructure holder's own record of the inauguration; it is the country's first terrestrial international route on this ledger.

subject: infra.connect
name: GETESA network modernisation
status: In development, slowed by payment arrears
milestone: Vice-President ordered the financing file expedited, 7 October 2026
position_start: An operator network with no published modernisation programme
position_end: The network expansion and optimisation agreement signed with the vendor in July 2026 has been slowed by Treasury payment arrears to the operator; the Vice-President instructed the finance ministry on 7 October 2026 to investigate and expedite the financing file, and the operator will cancel non-essential maintenance contracts until December to reinvest in the network
note: the independent press reports opaque procurement and overlapping state operators

subject: infra.connect
name: Governance index connectivity scores
milestone: 2024 edition of the index, scores for 2023
movement: No change, 2023 scores up 24.0 and 23.7 points over the decade
position_start: Mobile communications 28.3 of 100, 53rd of 54; internet and computers 32.6, 28th of 54 (2023)
position_end: Mobile communications 28.3 of 100, 53rd of 54 and up 24.0 points since 2014; internet and computers 32.6, 28th of 54 and up 23.7 points (2023)
note: composite index measures, not subscriber or user counts

subject: infra.connect
name: July-December 2026 connectivity plan
milestone: Semestral departmental plan presented to the Prime Minister, 15 July 2026
position_end: Presented, naming 2G and 4G coverage to 85% through 34 new towers in Annobon and the interior, Roaming Cero with Cameroon, Gabon, Chad and the Central African Republic, and a Sistema Nacional de Codigos Postales Digitales
note: the plan document itself is not held; this is a three-axis semestral plan distinct from the 35-objective consolidated plan

subject: infra.connect
name: Medusa submarine cable connection
milestone: Analysys Mason study of a landing at Bome or Bata
position_end: Under study, put at EUR 20-60m and 2029-30, with a Via Africa route also named
note: the existing ASD cable is reported to degrade quality, which is the stated reason for diversifying

subject: infra.connect
name: National internet exchange point
milestone: Reached construction stage in 2017
position_start: At construction stage with no launch recorded (2025-08)
position_end: The continental infrastructure registry records the exchange point reaching construction stage in 2017, with no launch, operator or traffic figure recorded since

subject: infra.connect
name: Nigeria-Equatorial Guinea subsea cable
milestone: Subsea fibre agreement signed, February 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Agreement signed, bundling a data centre; no route, capacity or delivery date published
sources: 2026-02-12-nigeria-equatorial-guinea-subsea-fibre|2026-02-24 Nigeria, Equatorial Guinea subsea cable strengthens connectivity

subject: infra.connect
name: Retail internet pricing
milestone: Operator promotion and regulator pricing order, 2026
position_start: Tariffs halved by government-operator agreement from 1 September 2022
position_end: The state operator raised data volumes 50 per cent across prepaid packages in August 2026 at held prices, its top tier reaching 24GB for 15,000 CFA; the regulator updated the primary and secondary broadband capacity market regime by ministerial order in February 2026

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink satellite internet service
milestone: Service confirmed available, 29 August 2026
position_start: Authorised temporarily for North American companies offshore operations inside jurisdictional waters, with extension to individual subscribers deferred on stated security grounds
position_end: The operator confirmed the satellite internet service is available in the country, following the opening of negotiations on national digital transformation in March 2026 and the temporary offshore authorisation of July 2026
note: the confirmation is the operator own, made on its and its owner social-media accounts; no licence, tariff, subscriber figure or type-approval record is held

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink service and its centralised distribution
milestone: Officially launched 2026-09-09
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The satellite internet service was officially launched on Wednesday 9 September 2026, announced by the vice-president. Sale and distribution are to be organised centrally: legal authority to sell rests with the state operator under the supervision of the Secretariat of State for Artificial Intelligence, with a dedicated bank account for the revenue, cancellation of contracts signed privately outside official channels, training of national technicians for installation and maintenance, and the competent departments instructed to work with the supplier to deactivate connections established beforehand.
note: announced through a vice-presidential statement and a session readout rather than a licence or regulation; no tariff, subscriber target, licence instrument or date for the deactivation of pre-existing connections is published

subject: infra.connect
name: TELGESA, the second state operator
milestone: Progress review with the investor agreement targeted for end-October 2026
position_start: Merger with Loita Group halted pending an audit of GECOMSA (2026-07)
position_end: The government reviewed progress in mid-October 2026 aiming to sign with the investor EGSA LOITA before the end of the month, with KPMG valuing GECOMSA's assets to fix the state's stake; launch before the end of 2026 depends on that valuation, financing and deployment of the 260 proposed towers
note: a Cyberteq audit presented in April 2026 found obsolete equipment, slow data speeds and congestion on the existing network

subject: infra.connect
name: ULTRAMAR submarine cable to Annobón
milestone: Annobón on the national fibre network, announced 2023-04-03
position_start: Not held
position_end: The state infrastructure operator GITGE resumed building the landing station of the cable from São Tomé to San Antonio de Palé in August 2022, after three years halted by the pandemic, and the island's connection to the national fibre network was announced on 3 April 2023; work began with a site study in 2016; no capacity figure is published

subject: infra.store
name: Government backup data centre works
milestone: Server room tender extended a third time, August 2026
position_start: A national data centre stood up under the public administration computerisation programme (2019-01)
position_end: A development bank-financed project tendered technical oversight of new backup data centre works to an international facility standard in June 2026, and the finance ministry's server room tender was extended for a third time to 16 September and remains unawarded (2026-08)

subject: infra.store
name: Government primary and backup data centres
milestone: PAMFP tender published for a Malabo primary and a Bata backup centre, June 2026
position_start: Data-economy actions including data centres validated with the World Bank (2025-12)
position_end: Tender published for a primary data centre in Malabo and a solar-powered backup in Bata for storage, processing and backup of public financial data

subject: infra.store
name: State broadcaster technical digitisation contract
milestone: Government formally pressed the supplier for outstanding equipment, August 2026
position_start: Contracted in 2020
position_end: The government has formally pressed the supplier to deliver the equipment still outstanding under the 2020 contract to digitise the state broadcaster’s technical infrastructure; no delivery schedule, contract value or penalty is on file
note: Six years after signature the contract is being chased rather than closed.

subject: infra.store
name: ZEEDE-GE digital economic zone at Djibloho
milestone: Creation under evaluation by the telecommunications ministry, March 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Under evaluation as a digital zone around AI, big data and high-performance data centres; no instrument, site or investment figure published

subject: infra.energy
name: Firms experiencing electrical outages
milestone: World Bank Enterprise Survey of 173 firms, May to September 2024
movement: No change, a first count with no earlier figure behind it
position_start: 33.3% of firms experienced outages, averaging 0.9 a month, against 69.7% across Sub-Saharan Africa (2024)
position_end: 33.3% of firms experienced outages, averaging 0.9 a month, against 69.7% across Sub-Saharan Africa (2024)
note: formal private firms with five or more employees only

subject: infra.energy
name: Power supply to network sites and data centres
milestone: Island generation audit finds the turbines inefficient, May 2026
position_start: Rural electrification near 2 per cent against 90 per cent urban (2025-07)
position_end: An audit by a foreign contractor found the island's gas turbines inefficient in May 2026 with an eighteen-month overhaul under study, and a mainland district records grid access at 2.4 per cent (2026-05)

subject: infra.energy
name: Rural electrification
milestone: Solar installations at a school and a clinic, April 2026
position_start: Rural electrification near 2 per cent against 90 per cent urban (2025-07)
position_end: A Chinese-backed foundation solar-powered a school and a clinic in April 2026 in a district where grid access stands at 2.4 per cent, and the Vice-President ordered a four-day study in March to extend the grid to a neighbouring town (2026-04)

subject: infra.energy
name: SEGESA grid fibre-optic modernisation proposal
milestone: Presented to the Vice-President's cabinet at Jefatura del Estado, Malabo, 21 May 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: SEGESA and Huawei proposal to replace copper with fibre optic in electrical substations for AI-based fault prediction and reduced fire risk, with spare capacity leased to telecom operators to extend national broadband coverage; under review, with the Vice-President citing a need for exhaustive analysis before viability is determined
note: timing coincides with a GETESA board reshuffle, raising the possibility of a joint SEGESA-GETESA-Huawei project; still a proposal, not a contract

subject: infra.capacity
name: Data centre capacity in service
milestone: Technical facilities described in GITGE's own factsheet, content dated internally to 2016-2017 despite a 2025-07 upload path
position_start: Not held
position_end: Two technical facilities, one in Bata and one in Malabo, each with two generators and ten nodes with distribution and transmission equipment, per GITGE's own factsheet; no floor-area, power or storage figure is given, and no later capacity figure is on record
note: as_at padded to the year only known (2016); the document's upload path is 2025-07 but its content narrates 2016 achieved and 2017 planned work per GITGE's own internal dating

subject: infra.capacity
name: In-house capacity to run the state networks
milestone: Maintenance to be brought in-house under the 2026-2030 plan
position_start: 2,315 civil servants trained under the first phase of public administration computerisation (2019-01)
position_end: The state operator's 2026-2030 plan orders it to cut tariffs, shift maintenance in-house and launch its own payment service; 80 technicians are to train in China under the surveillance contract annexes; and a security firm was hired in December 2025 to audit the networks (2026-07)

subject: infra.capacity
name: National centre for computerising the public administration (CNIAPGE)
milestone: Created by Decree 55/2013, operating since 2015
position_end: Charged with deploying and maintaining the administration's computing resources and the government's digital agenda; by May 2022 it ran the government data centre, had computerised 14 institutions and trained about 3,500 civil servants, on its director general's account

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Alleged leak of official documents of the Presidency of the Government
milestone: Named by the Vice-President on social media, reported 2026-10-09
position_start: No incident held
position_end: The Vice-President named the alleged members of a network leaking official documents of the Presidency of the Government, alleging that a registry official extracted several years of administrative files and handed a hard drive to a foreign national on the pretext of a project to digitise the Presidency's archives; it is presented as the largest leak of official documents in the country to date
note: the account is the government's own; no judicial finding is on file

subject: infra.cybersec

subject: data.statistics
name: Statistics from administrative records
milestone: Ninth national yearbook presented, 2026-09-25
position_start: Vital events compiled from hospital and community records into a first report (2024-10)
position_end: The eighth national statistical yearbook carries 19,586 civil servants, 10,468 online visas approved and public debt at 33.3 per cent of output, all from administrative sources; the population is still projected off the 2015 census (2025-10). The statistics institute began a ministry-by-ministry supervision tour of statistical services on 2 September 2026, starting at the interior and education ministries and running to 9 September, ordered by the national statistics council's eighth session of 27 August, to assess each service's state and consolidate the national statistical system (2026-09). The ninth yearbook, covering the last five years, was presented in Malabo on 25 September 2026, the institute naming weak administrative registers, undigitised processes and poor information-system interoperability among its outstanding challenges (2026-09)
note: no findings, service inventory or report from the tour is published, and the account is the institute's own
